```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r readModelDb("Calvier_2018_iv1cmt_dispersion")()$meta$reference`
* Description: `r readModelDb("Calvier_2018_iv1cmt_dispersion")()$meta$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s11095-018-2487-1>

Calvier et al. ask whether two hepatic PBPK parameters that cannot be
measured directly in children -- the whole-liver unbound intrinsic
clearance (CLint,u,WL) and the hepatic blood flow (Qh) -- can be
estimated by population modelling of clinical PK data. One drug cannot
separate them, because its plasma clearance is a single equation in two
unknowns. Two drugs metabolised by the same isoenzyme can, provided the
ratio of their intrinsic clearances (CLintratio, measurable in vitro) is
known: the two drugs then share the same Qh and the same CLint,u,WL.

The paper is a methodology study. Its PK content is a pair of
*hypothetical* drugs A and B, each infused to its own arm of 45
one-year-old children, whose plasma clearance follows the hepatic
dispersion model. That model is packaged here as a reusable design
template. All of its values are design constants chosen by the authors,
so all are `fixed()`; none is an estimate of a real molecule.

# Population

There are no real subjects. The design population is 1-year-old
children; the typical Qh of 20.3 L/h was obtained by the authors from
500 male and 500 female 1-year-olds simulated in Simcyp V15 (Methods,
Hypothetical Drug Combinations; Table III). The trial has two arms of
45 patients with seven samples each (Fig. 2).

```{r population-meta}
mod_fun <- readModelDb("Calvier_2018_iv1cmt_dispersion")
str(mod_fun()$meta$population, max.level = 1)
```

# Source trace

| Quantity | Value packaged | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Plasma clearance, dispersion model | `CLp = Qh * ER * B:P`, `ER = 1 - FH`, `FH = 4a / ((1+a)^2 exp((a-1)/(2DN)) - (1-a)^2 exp(-(a+1)/(2DN)))`, `a = sqrt(1 + 4 RN DN)`, `RN = (fu/B:P) CLint,u,WL / Qh` | Equations 1-6; Supplementary material 1 'Model equations'; Supplementary material 2 (PFIM model code) |
| Shared CLint, drug B = drug A x ratio | `CLint,u,WL_B = CLint,u,WL * CLintratio` | Equations 7-9 |
| One-compartment disposition per drug | `dA/dt = K0 - CL/V * A`, `C = A/V` | Supplementary material 1; Supplementary material 2 |
| `lqh` | log(20.30106) L/h | Supplementary material 3 `beta` QH = 0.338351 L/min; Table I 20.3 L/h |
| `lclint` | log(80.31137) L/h | Supplementary table 1 row with ER 0.94 (clint 1.338522914 L/min) |
| `clint_ratio` | 0.05818729 | Supplementary table 1 rows with ER 0.20 and 0.94 (0.077884914 / 1.338522914) |
| `dn` | 0.17 | Text after equation 6; Table I; Supplementary material 2 |
| `fu`, `fu_drugb`, `bp`, `bp_drugb` | 1 | Table I; Supplementary material 2 |
| `lvc`, `lvc_drugb` | log(4) L | Table I; Supplementary material 3 |
| `etalqh`, `etalclint` | 0.1 | Supplementary material 3 `omega` (scenario 'OMEGA QH = 0.1 & OMEGA CLINT = 0.1'); Table I ranges 0.1-0.6 and 0.1-0.8 |
| `etalvc`, `etalvc_drugb` | 0.25 | Table I; Supplementary material 3 |
| `propSd`, `propSd_drugb` | 0.1 | Table I; Supplementary material 3 `sig.slopeA` / `sig.slopeB` |
| Infusion rate | `CLp * 70 mg/L` | Clinical Trial Design; Supplementary table 1 (`k0 / CL = 70` on every row) |
| Sampling times | every half-life from 1 to 7 half-lives | Clinical Trial Design; Supplementary material 3 `protA` / `protB` |

```{r model}
mod <- mod_fun()
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
# The explicit ODEs must be the ones solved (no automatic linCmt solve).
stopifnot(is.null(mod$linCmt))
```

# Known-answer check: the dispersion model against the authors' drug table

Supplementary table 1 lists, for every hypothetical drug, the whole-liver
intrinsic clearance the authors fed to PFIM together with its extraction
ratio and plasma clearance (all per minute). Evaluating the packaged
model at those intrinsic clearances, with the deposited Qh, must return
the tabulated extraction ratios. The rows below are transcribed from the
supplement; they include the paper's two thresholds (ER 0.27 and 0.93)
and the two drugs packaged here (ER 0.20 and 0.94).

```{r er-known-answer}
supp_t1 <- data.frame(
  row = c(1, 10, 20, 21, 28, 42, 56, 70, 84, 94, 95, 100),
  clint_per_min = c(
    0.001696914, 0.032335914, 0.073423914, 0.077884914, 0.111228914,
    0.191892914, 0.300866914, 0.462498914, 0.751832914, 1.244823914,
    1.338522914, 2.604655914
  ),
  cl_per_min = c(
    0.001691472, 0.030452038, 0.064287123, 0.067670263, 0.091354766,
    0.138723934, 0.186093370, 0.233462589, 0.280831698, 0.314666866,
    0.318050407, 0.334967973
  ),
  er_published = c(
    0.004999155, 0.090001196, 0.190001006, 0.199999899, 0.269999598,
    0.409999480, 0.550000154, 0.690000185, 0.829999892, 0.929999950,
    0.940000027, 0.990000002
  )
)

# Evaluate the model's own clearance block at each tabulated CLint by
# setting lclint per row (typical values, both drugs at the same CLint).
er_grid <- supp_t1 |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = row_number())
ev_grid <- data.frame(
  id = er_grid$id, time = 0, amt = 0, evid = 0, dvid = 1L
)
params_grid <- data.frame(
  id = er_grid$id,
  lclint = log(er_grid$clint_per_min * 60),
  clint_ratio = 1
)
sol_grid <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typ, ev_grid,
  params = params_grid, returnType = "data.frame"
)
er_check <- er_grid |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    er_model = sol_grid$eh,
    cl_model_per_min = sol_grid$cl / 60
  )
knitr::kable(
  er_check |>
    dplyr::select(row, clint_per_min, er_published, er_model, cl_per_min, cl_model_per_min) |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Supp. table 1 row" = row,
      "CLint,u,WL (L/min)" = clint_per_min,
      "ER (published)" = er_published,
      "ER (model)" = er_model,
      "CLp (published, L/min)" = cl_per_min,
      "CLp (model, L/min)" = cl_model_per_min
    ),
  digits = 7
)
# Same equation, same inputs: the residual is the 7-9 digit rounding of
# the supplement, so a tight bound is correct here.
stopifnot(
  max(abs(er_check$er_model - er_check$er_published)) < 1e-5,
  max(abs(er_check$cl_model_per_min - er_check$cl_per_min)) < 1e-5
)
```

The packaged typical drugs have extraction ratios 0.94 (drug A) and 0.20
(drug B), the pair the authors used for their stochastic simulation and
estimation (Results, Step 3: Investigation of Bias):

```{r typical-er}
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typ,
  data.frame(id = 1, time = 0, amt = 0, evid = 0, dvid = 1L),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Drug = c("A", "B"),
    `Extraction ratio` = c(typ$eh, typ$eh_drugb),
    `CLp (L/h)` = c(typ$cl, typ$cl_drugb),
    `Half-life (h)` = log(2) * 4 / c(typ$cl, typ$cl_drugb),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  digits = 4
)
stopifnot(
  abs(typ$eh - 0.94) < 1e-5,
  abs(typ$eh_drugb - 0.20) < 1e-5
)
```

# Table III: extraction-ratio thresholds as plasma clearances

With fu and B:P equal to 1, equations 1-2 reduce to `CLp = Qh * ER`.
Table III uses that relation to convert the paper's two thresholds
(ER 0.27 and 0.93) into plasma clearances at eight ages, from the
Simcyp-derived Qh at each age.

```{r table3}
table3 <- data.frame(
  age = c("25 years", "15 years", "5 years", "2 years", "1 year", "6 months", "1 month", "1 day"),
  qh = c(87.0, 89.2, 41.5, 30.0, 20.3, 13.0, 7.5, 6.4),
  clp027_published = c(23.5, 24.1, 11.2, 8.1, 5.5, 3.5, 2.0, 1.7),
  clp093_published = c(80.9, 83.0, 38.6, 27.9, 18.9, 12.1, 7.0, 6.0)
)
table3 <- table3 |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    clp027_model = qh * 0.27,
    clp093_model = qh * 0.93
  )
knitr::kable(
  table3 |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Age" = age,
      "Qh (L/h)" = qh,
      "CLp at ER 0.27 (published)" = clp027_published,
      "CLp at ER 0.27 (model)" = clp027_model,
      "CLp at ER 0.93 (published)" = clp093_published,
      "CLp at ER 0.93 (model)" = clp093_model
    ),
  digits = 2
)
stopifnot(
  max(abs(round(table3$clp027_model, 1) - table3$clp027_published)) <= 0.1,
  max(abs(round(table3$clp093_model, 1) - table3$clp093_published)) <= 0.1
)
```

# Extraction ratio as a function of intrinsic clearance

The relationship the design exploits (the paper's Fig. 1 shows it
schematically): at low intrinsic clearance the plasma clearance tracks
CLint,u,WL, at high intrinsic clearance it saturates at Qh. Points are
the transcribed rows of Supplementary table 1.

```{r er-curve, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
clint_grid <- exp(seq(log(0.05), log(300), length.out = 200))
curve_sol <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typ,
  data.frame(id = seq_along(clint_grid), time = 0, amt = 0, evid = 0, dvid = 1L),
  params = data.frame(id = seq_along(clint_grid), lclint = log(clint_grid)),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
ggplot(data.frame(clint = clint_grid, er = curve_sol$eh), aes(clint, er)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(
    data = supp_t1,
    aes(clint_per_min * 60, er_published),
    colour = "firebrick"
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.27, 0.93), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Whole-liver unbound intrinsic clearance (L/h)",
    y = "Hepatic extraction ratio",
    caption = "Line: dispersion model at Qh = 20.3 L/h, DN = 0.17, fu = B:P = 1. Points: Supplementary table 1. Dashed: ER 0.27 and 0.93."
  )
```

# The two-arm design

Each arm receives one drug as a constant-rate infusion started at time
zero, with the rate set to `CLp * 70` so the typical patient approaches
70 mg/L, and is sampled once per typical half-life from the first to the
seventh. Rates and sampling times are design constants computed from the
typical drug, as in the authors' PFIM input file, not from each
individual.

```{r design}
cl_a <- typ$cl
cl_b <- typ$cl_drugb
thalf_a <- log(2) * 4 / cl_a
thalf_b <- log(2) * 4 / cl_b
rate_a <- cl_a * 70
rate_b <- cl_b * 70
infusion_dur <- 10 # h, longer than seven half-lives of either drug
stopifnot(7 * max(thalf_a, thalf_b) < infusion_dur)

make_arm <- function(ids, cmt, rate, obs_times, dvid) {
  dose <- data.frame(
    id = ids, time = 0, amt = rate * infusion_dur, rate = rate,
    evid = 1, cmt = cmt, dvid = NA_integer_
  )
  obs <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = dvid)
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}
```

## Typical-value profiles against the closed form

For the typical patient the solution is `C(t) = 70 * (1 - exp(-kel t))`,
so the solve must match it to numerical precision.

```{r typical-profile, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
grid_a <- sort(unique(c(0, seq(0, 7 * thalf_a, length.out = 141))))
grid_b <- sort(unique(c(0, seq(0, 7 * thalf_b, length.out = 141))))
ev_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_arm(1, "central", rate_a, grid_a, 1L) |> dplyr::mutate(arm = "Drug A (ER 0.94)"),
  make_arm(2, "central_drugb", rate_b, grid_b, 2L) |> dplyr::mutate(arm = "Drug B (ER 0.20)")
)
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typ, ev_typ |> dplyr::select(-arm),
  returnType = "data.frame", keep = "dvid"
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    arm = ifelse(id == 1, "Drug A (ER 0.94)", "Drug B (ER 0.20)"),
    conc = ifelse(id == 1, Cc, Cc_drugb),
    kel_typ = ifelse(id == 1, cl_a / 4, cl_b / 4),
    conc_closed = 70 * (1 - exp(-kel_typ * time))
  )
stopifnot(max(abs(sim_typ$conc - sim_typ$conc_closed)) < 1e-4)

ggplot(sim_typ, aes(time / ifelse(id == 1, thalf_a, thalf_b), conc, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (typical half-lives)",
    y = "Plasma concentration (mg/L)",
    colour = NULL,
    caption = "Typical-value profiles under the design infusion; both approach 70 mg/L."
  )
```

## Stochastic simulation of the trial (45 patients per arm)

```{r vpc, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20180914)
n_arm <- 45
ev_sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_arm(1:n_arm, "central", rate_a, thalf_a * 1:7, 1L),
  make_arm(n_arm + 1:n_arm, "central_drugb", rate_b, thalf_b * 1:7, 2L)
)
sim_rx <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_sim, keep = "dvid")
sim_par <- as.data.frame(sim_rx$params)
sim <- as.data.frame(sim_rx) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    id = as.integer(as.character(id)),
    arm = ifelse(id <= n_arm, "Drug A (ER 0.94)", "Drug B (ER 0.20)"),
    thalf = ifelse(id <= n_arm, thalf_a, thalf_b),
    n_half = round(time / thalf)
  )

vpc <- sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm, n_half) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), p50 = median(sim), p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(vpc, aes(n_half, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = sim, aes(n_half, sim), alpha = 0.2, size = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  labs(
    x = "Sample (typical half-lives after the start of the infusion)",
    y = "Plasma concentration (mg/L)",
    caption = "Median and 90% interval of 45 simulated patients per arm, with residual error."
  )
```

The two drugs respond very differently to the shared random effects.
Drug A (high ER) clearance follows the individual Qh almost one to one,
while drug B (low ER) clearance follows the individual CLint,u,WL; that
contrast is what makes the two parameters jointly estimable. The
correlations of the individual clearances with the shared random effects
show it:

```{r eta-sensitivity}
indiv <- sim |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::select(id, cl, cl_drugb) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    sim_par |>
      dplyr::mutate(id = as.integer(as.character(id))) |>
      dplyr::select(id, etalqh, etalclint),
    by = "id"
  )
stopifnot(nrow(indiv) == 2 * n_arm)
sens <- data.frame(
  Clearance = c("Drug A (ER 0.94)", "Drug B (ER 0.20)"),
  `cor(log CL, eta Qh)` = c(
    cor(log(indiv$cl), indiv$etalqh), cor(log(indiv$cl_drugb), indiv$etalqh)
  ),
  `cor(log CL, eta CLint)` = c(
    cor(log(indiv$cl), indiv$etalclint), cor(log(indiv$cl_drugb), indiv$etalclint)
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(sens, digits = 2)
# Structural, not a tail statistic: the high-ER drug is flow-limited and
# the low-ER drug capacity-limited.
stopifnot(
  sens[1, 2] > sens[1, 3],
  sens[2, 3] > sens[2, 2]
)
```

# NCA of the typical-value profiles (PKNCA)

The paper reports no NCA. As a numerical check, PKNCA is run on the
dense typical-value profiles over the seven-half-life sampling window and
compared with the closed-form AUC
`70 * (T - (1 - exp(-kel T)) / kel)` and the closed-form concentration at
`T = 7` half-lives, `70 * (1 - 2^-7)`.

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(conc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, conc, arm)
dose_df <- ev_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, arm)

end_time <- c(7 * thalf_a, 7 * thalf_b)
intervals <- data.frame(
  id = 1:2, start = 0, end = end_time,
  cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
)
o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, conc ~ time | arm + id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | arm + id)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = intervals))
nca_res <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  dplyr::select(arm, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)

kel_typ <- c(cl_a, cl_b) / 4
reference <- data.frame(
  arm = c("Drug A (ER 0.94)", "Drug B (ER 0.20)"),
  cmax = 70 * (1 - 2^-7),
  auclast = 70 * (end_time - (1 - exp(-kel_typ * end_time)) / kel_typ)
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-arm, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "reference")

nca_cmp <- nca_res |>
  dplyr::inner_join(reference, by = c("arm", "PPTESTCD")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (PPORRES - reference) / reference)
knitr::kable(
  nca_cmp |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Arm" = arm,
      "NCA parameter" = PPTESTCD,
      "PKNCA (typical value)" = PPORRES,
      "Closed form" = reference,
      "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
    ),
  digits = 3
)
stopifnot(max(abs(nca_cmp$pct_diff)) < 0.5)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Methodology model, no fitted estimates.** Every value is a design
  constant chosen by the authors; all are `fixed()`. The paper's own
  results are relative standard errors from PFIM (Fig. 3) and estimation
  errors from a NONMEM stochastic simulation and estimation with
  parameter uncertainty (Table IV); neither can be reproduced by a
  forward simulation and neither is a model parameter.
* **Which drug pair.** The paper's optimal-design step sweeps every
  pair of its hypothetical drugs; its stochastic simulation and
  estimation uses one pair, ER 0.94 and ER 0.2 in 1-year-olds. That pair
  is packaged, with the intrinsic clearances taken from the
  Supplementary table 1 rows whose ER is 0.94 and 0.20. Other pairs are
  obtained by changing `lclint` and `clint_ratio`.
* **Which drug is A.** The paper does not say which of the two
  simulation drugs was drug A. Table I gives CLintratio = CLint B /
  CLint A in the range 0.00065-0.97, i.e. drug B has the lower intrinsic
  clearance, so drug A is the ER 0.94 drug here. The deposited PFIM loop
  assigns A to the earlier row of the drug table (the lower ER), which
  gives ratios above 1; because drug B's intrinsic clearance is drug A's
  times a fixed ratio with the same random effect, the two assignments
  describe the same model.
* **Which variance scenario.** The paper evaluates four combinations of
  omega^2 for CLint,u,WL (0.1 or 0.8) and Qh (0.1 or 0.6) and, in the
  stochastic simulation, samples them uniformly over those ranges. The
  deposited PFIM input file carries the 0.1 / 0.1 scenario, which is
  packaged. Users exploring the paper's other scenarios should change
  `etalclint` and `etalqh`.
* **Constant-rate infusion as a dose event.** The PFIM model carries the
  infusion rate as a fixed parameter `K0` inside the ODE; here it is an
  ordinary infusion dose (`rate` and `amt`) into `central` or
  `central_drugb`, so the model file has no design constants in it.
* **Units.** The deposited PFIM files run in minutes (Qh 0.338351 L/min,
  intrinsic clearances in L/min); they are converted to hours. Dose is in
  mg and concentration in mg/L, consistent with the 70 mg/L target.
* **Drug count.** The methods text says 99 hypothetical drugs were
  generated; Supplementary table 1 has 100 rows (ER 0.005 to 0.99). This
  does not affect the packaged model.
* **Names.** Drug A takes the bare canonical names (`central`, `lvc`,
  `lclint`, `fu`, `bp`, `Cc`, `propSd`) and drug B the `_drugb` suffix,
  following the library's convention that the second analyte is
  suffixed. Qh and DN are shared by both drugs and carry no suffix.
